name: Papeta Ma Gosht
subtitle: everyday mutton and potato stew, gently spiced and thickened by the potatoes themselves
prepNotes: Cut the potatoes big — quarters, not chunks — or they will disintegrate before the mutton is done.
Keep the peeled potatoes in cold water until they go into the pan so they do not grey.
Take the mutton out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the chopped onion over medium heat until soft and pale gold, about 10 minutes.
steps.tip: This is a gentler dish than jardaloo ma gosht. Do not brown the onion hard.

steps.text: Add ginger and garlic paste with the slit green chillies and fry 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powder. Fry 30 seconds.
Add the mutton and brown 6 minutes, turning the pieces so each face colours.
Add the tomato and salt and cook 8 minutes until the tomato has broken down and the oil rises.
Pour in the water and simmer covered 45 minutes, or pressure cook 3 whistles and release naturally.
Add the potatoes, cover, and cook 20 minutes more until a knife slides through them with no resistance.
steps.tip: Crush two potato pieces against the side of the pan — that is what thickens the gravy.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala and simmer uncovered 5 minutes to reduce to a pouring consistency.
Finish with coriander leaves and the lemon juice, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rotli or plain rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat over low heat with a little water; the potatoes soak up gravy overnight, so expect to loosen it.
